title: rice-scorecard template variables
description: Values for templates/rice-scorecard.md.j2 and templates/rice-scorecard.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from rice-scorecard.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

actual.title: Actual
actual.description: The actual used under 'Post-Ship Actuals (fill in after delivery)'.

confidence_policy.title: Confidence policy
confidence_policy.description: What each confidence level means here - what evidence earns 100 percent rather than 50. Without a shared rule, confidence quietly becomes how much the author likes the feature.

effort_unit.title: Effort unit
effort_unit.description: The unit for the effort column, one for the whole sheet. A table mixing days and months produces a ranking that is arithmetically meaningless and looks perfectly reasonable.

product_name.description: The product these features belong to. Scores from two products in one table are not comparable - reach means different populations and effort means different teams.

quarter.title: Quarter
quarter.description: The planning period this covers, e.g. "Q4 2026". RICE scores only compare inside one period; carrying last quarter's reach forward is how a stale estimate wins a slot it should not.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the reach numbers come from - the analytics query, the report, the proxy metric and why it stands in. Reach is the input people invent most freely, so name the source once for the whole sheet.

veto_rationale.title: Veto rationale
veto_rationale.description: If you overrode the ranking, say why - the moat, the contract, the bet RICE cannot encode. Overriding is legitimate; overriding silently is what teaches everyone the scores are theatre.
